source.title: An overview of condensation phenomenon in deep learning
source.authors: Z. Xu; Yaoyu Zhang; Zhang-Chen Zhou

record.file_problem: The text contains the full paper, including sections, figures and references. Some findings are described from cited work rather than tested by this overview.
record.tranche_reason: The overview reports its own experiments on trained networks and test accuracy, which bear on the coexistence of fitting natural labels and generalization (V1), but it does not test the claim's full random-label comparison.
record.gate_note: Own experiments measure neuron condensation and, in one MNIST CNN experiment, training and test accuracy. The width and dropout generalization statements are summaries of cited studies, not this overview's own results; they are not rows. Reported benchmark accuracies for pretrained ResNet18 likewise are not tied to a training-versus-test gap measurement.
record.test_reason: The study's own experiments measure neuron condensation and training dynamics. R1 reports natural-label training and test accuracy, but no random-label experiment establishes the memorization capacity required by V1. No own result tests the comparisons specified by V2–V8; relevant background findings are attributed to other studies.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors present condensation as a common but condition-dependent tendency during nonlinear training, discuss mechanisms and possible implications for generalization and reasoning, and acknowledge that understanding remains preliminary. They do not establish V1's random-label versus natural-label comparison.
record.recipe_differences: Overview of prior work with illustrative experiments on condensation; it does not reproduce the original claim's random-label and natural-label comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization scale, architecture, layer, optimizer, dropout rate, and training stage are discussed as affecting condensation; the paper does not measure their effects on the V1 training–test gap.

fits_no_version.finding: A single-layer CNN reaches 100% training accuracy and 97.62% test accuracy on natural-label MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A CNN with small initialization can fit MNIST's training labels perfectly while retaining high held-out accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Own experiments show neuron condensation varying with initialization, architecture, layer and training stage.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: During nonlinear training, neurons tend to form groups with similar outputs, with the degree of condensation depending on training conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 50 trials per width, wider two-layer ReLU networks spend more training epochs at lower training losses in a synthetic-function task.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing width changes optimization dynamics and can facilitate reaching lower training losses.

record.problems: V1's defining random-label control is absent. The MNIST CNN report gives no uncertainty estimates, and the accuracy result is stated in a figure caption rather than a comparison designed to isolate the claimed mechanism. Other overview findings are largely summaries of cited studies.
record.rows_left_out: No other own numerical result directly measures a version's training–test gap. Condensation figures and described results do not measure the generalization gap named by the versions; cited studies' results are excluded.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting capacity and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe, including chance-level held-out accuracy with random labels.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error. Section 7.2 measures training-loss distributions instead.
Held-out performance comparisons between convolutional and fully connected networks, including the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance under specified tuning budgets.
Large-versus-small-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout's effect on held-out classifier error. The reproduced dropout experiments concern condensation and synthetic-function fitting.
Association between magnitude-aware sharpness and generalization gaps, including comparisons with other measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V1 support verdict. High natural-label test accuracy alone does not test the defining coexistence claim. Cited and reproduced findings about dropout, width and transformer reasoning should retain their attribution rather than become this overview's independent evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test random-label fitting or chance-level test accuracy; does not evaluate the small Inception, AlexNet, MLP, or ImageNet settings named in the version.

rows.subject: single-layer CNN
rows.stage_stated: training until 100% accuracy on the training set
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with cross-entropy loss using Adam and full-batch training; continued until training accuracy reached 100%.

conditions.value: convolutional and fully connected layers initially follow N (0, 96−8 )

rows.measure: Accuracy on training and test sets
rows.value: 100% accuracy on the training set; test set accuracy is 97.62%
rows.note: Reports natural-label training and held-out accuracy, but does not compare against random labels or state chance accuracy.
rows.check: The reported 100% training accuracy and 97.62% test accuracy are correct. However, fitting natural labels does not establish capacity to fit random labels, so this row cannot measure V1's coexistence claim. The missing comparison is not evidence of a partial effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The model reaches 100% training accuracy and 97.62% test accuracy on MNIST (R1); the random-label comparison in V1 is untested.
